title: Three Booked After Muslim Biryani Seller Assaulted in Lucknow Over Beef Allegation
excerpt: Rizwan, 40, was attacked while carrying meat on his scooter in the Itaunja area; police seized the meat and sent samples for veterinary testing. No arrests had been made when the FIR was registered.
body:
• Rizwan, a 40-year-old biryani stall owner, was allegedly assaulted by three youths in Lucknow's Itaunja area on September 20 after they accused him of carrying beef while he transported meat on his scooter.
  • Police registered an FIR against the three accused — identified as Rana Yadav, Shanu, and Suraj — on charges including criminal intimidation, voluntarily causing hurt, and attempting to commit culpable homicide; no arrests had been made at the time of the report.
  • The seized meat has been sent to a veterinary officer for examination, and police say further action will depend on the laboratory findings.
  • A video purportedly showing the assault was widely circulated on social media, showing Rizwan being pushed to the ground and beaten by a mob.

A 40-year-old Muslim biryani stall owner was brutally assaulted in Lucknow's Itaunja area on the morning of September 20, 2026, after three youths accused him of carrying beef, police said. The victim, identified as Rizwan, a resident of Kasai Mohalla, runs a biryani stall near Badi Masjid in Mahona on Sundays and Thursdays and was carrying meat for his shop on a scooter when he was stopped.

According to the police complaint, the three accused — all in their 20s, identified as Rana Yadav, Shanu, and Suraj — allegedly assaulted Rizwan and threatened to kill him. A video purportedly showing the attack was widely circulated on social media: it shows Rizwan being pushed, grabbed, and forced to the ground while members of a mob, including a man wearing a saffron headscarf, kick and beat him. Local residents intervened as the situation turned tense, according to Madhyamam's reporting.

Injuries, FIR, and seized meat

Rizwan suffered injuries to his head and face and was discharged from the hospital on Sunday evening after receiving treatment, The Quint reported. Based on his written complaint, police registered an FIR against the three accused at the Itaunja police station.

The accused have been booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to criminal intimidation, intentional insult intended to provoke a breach of peace, voluntarily causing hurt, and attempting to commit culpable homicide, according to Maktoob's account. Police said the meat Rizwan was carrying had been seized and samples collected and sent to the veterinary officer for examination. Inspector Vinod Kumar of Itaunja police station said the situation at the spot remained peaceful and that law and order was under control.

The law around meat in Uttar Pradesh

The assault fits a recurring pattern in parts of Uttar Pradesh in which individuals transporting meat — frequently Muslim traders in the legal buffalo-meat supply chain — are stopped by groups acting on suspicion of cow slaughter or beef transport. Slaughter of cows and trade in cow meat are prohibited under the Uttar Pradesh Prevention of Cow Slaughter Act, 1955, as amended, which carries significant penalties including imprisonment and fines. Buffalo meat, by contrast, is legal to produce, transport, and trade in the state, subject to licensing and other regulations. Rizwan's account holds that he was transporting meat for legitimate food use, and one report references his clarification involving buffalo meat.

A tense weekend for meat sellers

The Lucknow assault was not the only flashpoint of the weekend. In Prayagraj's Phulpur area, members of the VHP-Bajrang Dal allegedly created a ruckus with local Muslim meat sellers after accusing them of selling beef, according to Madhyamam and Maktoob. And in Kaushambi district, police arrested three women after a raid on a private residence over allegations that beef was being cooked there; samples from that seizure were also sent for forensic testing, with the women remanded to judicial custody.

What's next

Police say the exact circumstances of the Lucknow confrontation are under investigation and that further action will depend on the veterinary laboratory's findings on the seized meat. With no arrests made at the time of reporting, the question now is whether the FIR — which includes the serious charge of attempting to commit culpable homicide — leads to custody of the accused, and whether the lab report settles the question of what Rizwan was actually carrying. For now, the incident stands as another test of how Uttar Pradesh polices the line between enforcing its cattle-slaughter ban and protecting lawful traders from mob violence.
